Theme

Household, washing & chores

butler noun

also house steward, major-domo, head servant, steward (of a house)

classical

Plaut. Ps. 609: Quasi tē dīcās ātriēnsem.
Cic. Par. 5.38 (Lewis & Short)

ātriēnsis, ātriēnsis m.

noun, third declension

the slave in charge of the ātrium and so of the house: the steward

From ātrium.

Examples

  • Condus prōmus sum, prōcūrātor penī. — Quasi tē dīcās ātriēnsem. — Immō ātriēnsī ego imperō.

    I am the keeper and giver-out of the stores, the manager of the larder. — As if to say you were the steward. — No, I give the steward his orders.Plaut. Ps. 608b–609b

See also slave, doorkeeper, manager, provisions.

SourcesLewis & Short: atriensis

Plautus, Pseudolus 608b–609b.
